subject: Hexadecimal alphanumeric literals (mapping for non-existing corresponding character)
notes: §8.3.3.2.4 5) (cite.py OK) leaves the no-corresponding-character result to the implementor. DecodeHex maps each 2-digit group to the storage-byte law's character (U+00hh, FF = U+FFFF); HexGroupViolation refuses a partial group per §8.3.3.2.3 6) (cite.py OK). Probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s3/probe/p95.cob at 2014/2023: X"80FF0041" ORD 129 256 1 66, LENGTH 4 (before PB2919). Every group has a character, so the row states the case cannot arise. No spec-derived test pins the high-range values; test-ref empty. Closes the item-95 documentation gap owned by kb/Work/PB1397. PB2919 (train 1056, 2026-10-10): DecodeHex now images each 2-digit group by the storage-byte law (StorageByte.ToChar), so a group hh is U+00hh for 00 through FE and X"FF" is U+FFFF, HIGH-VALUE, the same character the byte 0xFF of a binary item reads as; ORD(X"80FF0041") is 129 65536 1 66 (golden 2002/pb2919_hex_literal_ff_is_the_storage_byte, unit StorageByteLawDriftTests).
